title: Stop the status page from showing a window that ends before it starts

blocks.text: The status page shows tonight's maintenance window, and the deploy gate refuses deploys inside it. Operators move the window from the admin console while thousands of page views read it. A few times a week a customer sends a screenshot of a window from 10:00 to 03:00, and once a cancelled window came back as "until 11:00" with no start.
`MaintenanceSchedule` already reschedules correctly. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/MaintenanceSchedule.java`:

items: `current()`: the window as it stands, for the page and the gate;

blocks.text: When you're done, a page view always shows a window that an operator actually scheduled (or `Window.NONE`), however it lines up with a reschedule, and a cancel never leaves part of a window behind. About five lines in total.
The constructor's `midReschedule` hook runs in the middle of `reschedule`; the tests use it to pause a reschedule halfway and make calls from other threads while it waits.

cases.says: a window rescheduled on another thread is the window the schedule then returns
after a cancel there is no window, and the next reschedule sets one again
a read made while a reschedule is halfway through returns the old window or the new one, never the new start with the old end
a cancel made while a reschedule is halfway through waits for it, so no end survives without its start

origin.section: A Reader That Skips the Lock Can See Two Fields That Were Never Written Together

concepts: A lock on a different object neither excludes the writer nor gives an edge to its writes, even when both methods are synchronized.
A reader that skips the lock can run between a locked writer's writes and see two fields that were never written together; reading under the same lock prevents it.
